title: Specify certificate table tuples and external proof replay bindings
description: §12.1 expected table has only {table:[...]}; no row/full-tuple encoding or borrowed-frame output binding is specified. External program hashes have no resolver protocol in this crate; structural subclaim schemas do not define cross-object retrieval. Decide ordered full output tuples in §12.2 enumeration versus explicit input/output keyed rows; pin clean/borrowed/region coordinates and frame endpoints. title: Decide opaque imported workspace proof summaries
description: §6.1 specifies call provenance; §6.2 requires the exact computing sequence; §9.3 defines resolution/validation but no producer-side proof-summary protocol. Decide signature-only uninterpreted extensional call identities with exact forward/adjoint histories versus linked body/certificate obligations for workspace spanning opaque calls (unlinked hash remains possible). First requires canonical call keys and cell versions; second requires pending-obligation API and linked replay. No permission to reject imported capability permanently. See opaque-workspace section of docs/design/2026-10-30-m2-open-proofs.md.

title: Decide general symbolic workspace and action CFG proof contract
description: ISA §6.2 binds cleanup to its exact computing sequence; §5.3 defines structured action bodies but not multi-block control flow. Decide canonical versioned symbolic history (uninterpreted token/argument-dependent calls, explicit path state) versus per-specialisation proof obligations plus structured-only serialized actions. The first needs a shared symbolic IR and path/join semantics; the second needs an explicit universal coverage contract and must never turn samples into proof. Ordinary cross-call workspace is an implementation design gap, not an ISA impossibility. See docs/design/2026-10-30-m2-open-proofs.md, symbolic-workspace section. Retain loud refusal until decision and red-green universal implementation.
